paragraphs: The early shift begins with instrument calibration. During the day, follow inspection routes through the facility and surrounding areas, checking probes and collecting water and air samples. At midday, review reading trends. Immediately verify and report anomalies. Before leaving, archive data and hand over to the night shift.

In short, they monitor environmental radiation. Work includes deploying probes, inspecting, sampling, reading data, reporting anomalies, and maintaining equipment. Combining analysis with field work, they serve on the front line of safety.
